explanation: A little hagfish slime swells in seawater into a big mass of gooey threads. Afterwards the hagfish ties itself in a knot and slides it along its body to wipe itself clean.

claims.text: Hagfish release slime that can clog the gills of predators such as sharks, making them let go.
Moray eels, lampreys and electric eels do not defend themselves with gill-clogging slime.
Hagfish slime expands greatly in seawater into a mass of fibrous threads.
Hagfish tie themselves in knots to scrape slime off their bodies.
